form.name: Name
form.publicScoreboardHint: (lists this competition on <link>/public</link> and lets anyone view the board without an account)
form.ctftimeHint: (exposes a CTFtime-format feed so the event can be rated on ctftime.org)
form.bracketsHint: Parallel rankings competitors self-select (e.g. Students, Open). Leave empty for a single ranking.
form.maxTeamSizeHint: Members allowed per team. Blank = unlimited.
form.controlsIntro: Run-day controls plus the schedule. The three controls apply immediately; the schedule at the bottom saves with the form.
form.statusHint: Competitors can play only while running — otherwise challenges show a closed message (the final scoreboard stays visible after it ends). The schedule below moves this automatically; Start / Stop override it now.
form.startConfirmDescription: Competitors will immediately be able to view challenges, submit flags, and see the scoreboard.
form.stopConfirmDescription: Challenge viewing and submissions close for competitors right away; the scoreboard stays visible as final standings. You can start it again later. Want a temporary stop instead? Pause the competition rather than stopping it.
form.pauseHint: Temporarily halt gameplay — competitors can't submit flags (staff still can, to test). Instantly reversible, and separate from stopping (which ends the competition) or freezing the board.
form.freezeHint: Freeze the public board at its current standings — competitors keep solving and their points still count, but the board stops showing movement until you unfreeze it. Staff still see live standings.
form.freezeConfirmDescription: Competitors keep solving and their points still count — the public board just stops showing movement until you unfreeze it. Staff can still view live standings.
form.scheduleHint: When play auto-starts / ends and when registration is open. Saved with the form; a manual Start / Stop above overrides these.
form.rulesOverrideHintTeam: Supersedes the site-wide rules for this competition. Leave empty to use the site-wide document (Admin → Site settings). Unless display-only is on, users must accept the effective rules before they can join or create/join a team.
form.rulesOverrideHintIndividual: Supersedes the site-wide rules for this competition. Leave empty to use the site-wide document (Admin → Site settings). Unless display-only is on, users must accept the effective rules before they can join.
form.displayOnlyHint: — show the rules at join without requiring an explicit “I accept” (nothing blocks the join).
form.rulesFootnote: Saving a new or changed override prompts every participant to accept the rules again. Staff with competition-edit access never see the prompt.
form.rulesConfirmDescription: Saving a new or changed rules override clears all existing acceptances — every participant will be prompted to accept the rules again before they can continue.

form.mcGuessLimitHint: Guesses each competitor (or team) gets per multiple-choice question, to curb brute-forcing. Blank = unlimited. Applies competition-wide.
form.mcPenaltyHint: Each wrong guess on a multiple-choice question lowers its value for that team/competitor by this percent, so a later correct answer awards less (floored at 0). Blank = off. Pairs with the guess limit.

settings.rulesHeadingDescription: The site-wide document users accept before joining a competition.

settings.aiHeadingDescription: Connect an OpenAI-compatible provider to power the read-only organiser assistant.
settings.instancesHeadingDescription: Point Flagpost at a container runtime so challenges can hand each team an isolated, running instance.
settings.registrationDescription: Whether anyone can sign up. When closed, only an administrator can create accounts (Admin → Users).
settings.usernameChangesDescription: Whether accounts can rename themselves from the profile page (subject to the rename cooldown). Off pins usernames to what was issued — an administrator can still rename any account from Admin → Users.

settings.updateChecksDescription: Once a day Flagpost asks updates.flagpost.io whether a newer release exists. The request sends only the version you're running — no identifier, no hostname, no competition or user data — and the count of those requests is how the project gauges how many deployments are live. See PRIVACY.md for the full detail.
settings.updatesOff: Off — never contact the update service
settings.updateUnreachable: Running version {version}. Couldn't reach the update service — that's expected on an air-gapped install.
settings.updateError: Running version {version}. The update service responded but the answer wasn't usable.
settings.updateNever: Running version {version}. No check has run yet — the first one happens within a minute of startup.
settings.updateAvailable: Running version {version}. Version {latest} is available. Last checked {checked}.
settings.updateAvailableDismissed: Running version {version}. Version {latest} is available. You've dismissed the notice for it. Last checked {checked}.
settings.updateCurrent: Running version {version} — up to date. Last checked {checked}.
settings.updateCurrentStale: Running version {version} — up to date. Last checked {checked}. The most recent attempt failed.
settings.dataRetentionDescription: When on, an archived competition is permanently deleted — database records and stored files — once it has stayed archived for the retention period. The archive dialog shows the exact deletion date; unarchiving cancels the clock. Competitions archived before enabling this are never auto-deleted.
settings.autoDeleteOn: On — delete after the retention period
settings.emailAllowlistDescription: Restrict public sign-up to specific email domains. A rejected sign-up sees a generic error — it never learns which domains are allowed. Applies to public registration only; admin-created accounts and existing users' emails are unaffected. Enabling this makes email mandatory at registration.
settings.allowlistOn: On — only allowed domains may register
settings.emailVerificationDescription: Require a self-registered account to confirm its email (a link sent via the SMTP server below) before it can join a competition. Requires SMTP to be configured. Admin-created accounts (Admin → Users) are exempt, and turning this on never affects members who already joined.
settings.verificationOff: Off — anyone who registers can join
settings.smtpDescription: Used by the automation <mono>send_email</mono> action. Leave the host blank to disable email (the action becomes a no-op).

instances.providerDescription: Flagpost never mounts the Docker socket directly — point it at a least-privilege socket proxy (see docs/CHALLENGE_INSTANCES.md). The endpoint is a trusted operator setting, so it isn't subject to the outbound-request blocklist a private address needs.
instances.statusOff: Off — no instances can be launched
instances.endpointHint: The socket-proxy address, e.g. http://socket-proxy:2375. Never a raw Docker socket.
instances.publicHostHint: The hostname or IP competitors connect to for TCP challenges.
instances.registryCredentialHint: Base64 X-Registry-Auth for private challenge images. Leave blank for public images. Stored encrypted; write-only.
instances.exposureDescription: The host TCP port range instances are published on (open these in your firewall), and whether instances may reach the internet.
instances.egressDeny: Deny — instances can't reach the internet (default)
instances.egressAllow: Allow — instances may reach the internet
instances.egressHint: Deny requires the instance network to be internal; the network-isolation test verifies it.
instances.limitsDescription: Per-instance ceilings applied unless a challenge overrides them.
instances.setBeforeEnabling: Set an endpoint URL and public host before enabling instances.
instances.portRangeInvalid: The port range minimum can't exceed the maximum.
instances.testSaveFirst: Save an endpoint and public host first
instances.chalBaseDomainHint: Base domain for HTTP-exposed instances — each gets a per-instance subdomain (e.g. https://a1b2c3d4.chal.example.org). Requires wildcard DNS + a wildcard TLS cert. Leave blank to disable HTTP.
instances.spawnRateHint: Max launches per participant within the window, across all challenges. 0 disables the throttle.
instances.k8sTokenBeforeEnabling: Store a Kubernetes service-account token before enabling instances.
instances.k8sDescription: Connect to a Kubernetes cluster through a namespace-scoped service account. One namespace holds every instance, and the token needs only namespaced rights — Test connection checks that posture.
instances.k8sNamespaceHint: The namespace every per-instance Deployment, Service, Ingress and NetworkPolicy lives in. Create it plus its Role and service account from k8s/instances-rbac.yaml first.
instances.k8sTokenHint: Bearer token for the namespace-scoped service account. Write-only — stored encrypted and never shown again.
instances.k8sCaCertHint: PEM CA bundle that signs the API server's certificate. Leave blank to use the system trust store.
instances.k8sClusterCidrHint: Comma-separated pod/service ranges to keep unreachable from instances (peers + the control plane), e.g. 10.42.0.0/16,10.43.0.0/16. Optional but recommended.

ai.providerDescription: Point Flagpost at any OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint — a hosted API or a local model (Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio). The model must support tool calling; the assistant answers entirely through read-only tools. The base URL is a trusted operator setting, so it is not subject to the outbound-request blocklist a local address needs.
ai.removeStoredKey: Remove the stored key (use a keyless endpoint)
ai.keyNotSet: Not set — leave blank for a keyless endpoint
ai.responseLimitsDescription: Caps that bound each answer's length and how long Flagpost waits on the provider — the guardrails against a slow endpoint or a runaway token bill.
ai.adminPromptDescription: An optional override for the assistant's system prompt. It governs tone and focus only — the assistant is read-only and every tool re-checks your permissions, so no wording can widen what it can see. Leave blank to use the built-in prompt.
ai.testSaveFirst: Save a base URL and model first
ai.setBeforeEnabling: Set a base URL and model before enabling the AI module

authProviders.descLdap: Point Flagpost at your directory. Directory users sign in with the ordinary username & password form — no separate button appears. New providers start disabled.
authProviders.descSaml: Register Flagpost as a Service Provider at your IdP (its metadata is at the SP metadata URL below once saved), then paste the IdP's details here. New providers start disabled.
authProviders.descOauth: Register Flagpost as an OAuth client at your provider first, then paste its details here. New providers start disabled.
authProviders.protocolHint: Fixed after creation. OIDC suits most modern providers; plain OAuth 2.0 is for providers without OpenID Connect, like GitHub and Discord, where identity comes from a userinfo API call; SAML suits campus/enterprise IdPs (Shibboleth, ADFS); LDAP binds directly against a directory (AD, OpenLDAP, FreeIPA).
authProviders.displayNameHintLdap: Shown in the admin list — LDAP has no login button.
authProviders.displayNameHint: Shown on the login button: “Sign in with {name}”.
authProviders.slugHintEditing: Fixed after creation — it's part of the URLs registered at your provider.
authProviders.slugHint: Lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens. Appears in the callback/ACS URL.
authProviders.startTls: Upgrade with StartTLS (required for ldap:// — a plaintext connection is never used)
authProviders.bindDnHint: Used to look up the person's entry before their own credentials are checked. Its password goes in the bind password field below.
authProviders.ldapAttrHint: Login attribute: what people type as their username (<mono>sAMAccountName</mono> on AD, <mono>uid</mono> elsewhere). Stable ID: the attribute that identifies the account forever — <mono>objectGUID</mono> on AD, <mono>entryUUID</mono> on OpenLDAP/FreeIPA. Never a DN.
authProviders.idpSsoUrlHint: The HTTP-Redirect single-sign-on endpoint we send the login request to.
authProviders.idpCertHint: Every assertion is verified against this before it's trusted — the load-bearing setting.
authProviders.spEntityIdHint: Our identifier at the IdP. Must match what you register there.
authProviders.samlAttrHint: The exact SAML attribute names your IdP sends. The stable NameID (must be persistent) becomes the account's identity.
authProviders.userinfoUrlHint: There is no ID token in plain OAuth 2.0 — the account's identity is read from this endpoint's JSON response.
authProviders.claimMapHint: Which fields of the userinfo response carry identity. The subject must be the provider's stable user ID, never the email address — it's what keeps an account attached when the user renames or changes address upstream.
authProviders.verifiedEmailsUrlHint: For providers that keep verified addresses on a separate endpoint (GitHub). Only the primary, verified address is trusted. Leave blank if the userinfo response already carries a verified flag.
authProviders.usePkceHint: Extra protection where the provider supports it (Discord does; GitHub's OAuth Apps ignore it). Leave off if sign-in fails with an unexpected-parameter error.
authProviders.issuerUrlHint: Must be HTTPS and publicly resolvable. Discovery reads <mono>{url}</mono>.
authProviders.tenantTemplateHint: Multi-tenant Microsoft Entra only — leave blank for a normal provider. When set, the token's issuer is validated against this template with the signing-in tenant's GUID substituted for <mono>'{tenantid}'</mono>. Trusts every Entra tenant, so restrict access with the registration email-domain allowlist.
authProviders.secretHintLdap: Stored encrypted. The service account's password — required before the provider can be enabled.
authProviders.secretHintSaml: Stored encrypted. Only needed to sign our requests — leave blank otherwise.
authProviders.secretHintOidc: Stored encrypted. Leave blank for a public client using PKCE only.
authProviders.postureOpen: Open — public provider, registration rules apply
authProviders.postureClosed: Closed — being in this directory is the admission
authProviders.postureHintOpen: For public IdPs (Google, GitHub): new accounts pass the same registration-open and email-domain checks as the sign-up form.
authProviders.postureHintClosed: For your own directory (corporate or campus IdP): anyone who can sign in there may enter, even while public registration is closed.
authProviders.trustEmailHint: Lets a first sign-in attach to an existing account with the same address. Only enable this if the directory verifies mailbox ownership — an unverified address here can claim someone else's account.
authProviders.providerAdded: Provider added — enable it when you've tested it
authProviders.heading: Auth providers
authProviders.headingDescription: Let people sign in with an external identity provider. Local passwords keep working, so an administrator can still get in if a provider goes down.
authProviders.quickSetupHint: Each of these needs an app registered on the provider's side. After saving, register the callback URL Flagpost shows you.
authProviders.ldapSignInNote: Signs in through the standard username & password form
authProviders.deleteDescription: Anyone who signs in only through this provider will lose their way in — a single-sign-on account has no password to fall back on. Disabling it instead is reversible.
authProviders.emptyDescription: Add an OIDC, OAuth 2.0, SAML or LDAP provider to let people sign in with an existing account instead of a Flagpost password.
